lines.text: Your microwave doesn't heat your food. It shakes it.
Inside, an invisible field flips direction billions of times a second.
And water molecules are lopsided. One end's a little positive, the other a little negative.
So every flip yanks them around.
They spin, they slam into their neighbors, and that jostling... That's heat.
But the waves only reach about an inch in.
The middle has to wait for heat to creep inward. That's your frozen center.
And ice is even worse. Its molecules are locked in place, so they can't spin.
That's why defrost pulses on and off, giving the heat time to spread.
So no, it's not heating your food. It's shaking it.
